# Sec. 2102. Reconductoring and other activities in existing rights-of-way

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2102)

## Summary

Adds Federal Power Act section 216A: work that maintains or increases grid capacity inside an existing right-of-way (reconductoring, higher operating voltage, added circuits, advanced transmission technologies, added storage at an existing facility, a parallel circuit) is categorically excluded from NEPA, is not a major federal action, and is not an undertaking under the National Historic Preservation Act. It also amends Natural Gas Act section 7 so that repair, replacement, looping, compression and capacity-enhancement of interstate gas pipelines inside an existing right-of-way or previously reviewed footprint are not major federal actions or historic-preservation undertakings.

## Key points

- Reconductoring and in-corridor grid upgrades exempt from NEPA and NHPA section 106 ([p. 201, line 23 to p. 202, line 2](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=201))
- Gas pipeline looping and compression in existing corridors exempt from NEPA and NHPA section 106 ([p. 204, line 17 to p. 204, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=204))
- Clean Water Act and Clean Air Act requirements for pipelines stay in place ([p. 205, line 1 to p. 205, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=205))

## Selected statutory quotes

> Activities to maintain or increase the capacity of the electric grid within a covered area, and any Federal agency action authorizing such activities— “(A) are a category of actions designated as being categorically excluded

[p. 201, line 19 to p. 201, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=201)

Grid upgrades inside an existing right-of-way are excluded from NEPA.

> The term ‘covered activity’ means any repair, maintenance, replacement, upgrade, rebuilding, modification, optimization, minor relocation, looping, compression, capacity-enhancement project, or addition to a covered facility.

[p. 203, line 17 to p. 203, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=203)

The same exemption for gas pipeline work, including looping and compression.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

DOE and other agencies have administrative categorical exclusions for some reconductoring; there is no statutory exclusion, and pipeline looping and compression get FERC environmental review.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 (sec. 209) only told Interior and Agriculture to adopt categorical exclusions for in-corridor grid work, which survives as section 2214. The statutory exemptions here, including the gas pipeline one, are new.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2103. Transmission planning

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2103)

## Summary

Adds Federal Power Act sections 224 and 225. The Energy Department studies transmission constraints and congestion every 3 years and may identify constrained geographic areas. FERC must issue a rule within 180 days requiring every planning region to file a regional planning process and joint interregional processes with its neighbors within 2 years, updated every 4 years. The processes must use common assumptions, a fixed list of six benefits, and selection criteria of improved reliability, consumer benefit and public interest.

Costs are allocated to beneficiaries roughly commensurate with benefits. Compliance with the FERC planning orders published on June 11, 2024, December 6, 2024 and April 28, 2025 (Order 1920 and its two rehearing orders) counts as compliance for regional planning. A project selected in a regional or interregional plan is deemed to meet most of the findings for a FERC backstop permit. Approving a planning process is not a major federal action under NEPA.

## Key points

- Requires interregional transmission planning by statute ([p. 211, line 19 to p. 212, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=211))
- FERC rule in 180 days; regional filings in 2 years ([p. 211, line 11 to p. 211, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=211))
- Compliance with FERC's 2024 and 2025 planning orders (Order 1920) counts for the regional piece ([p. 217, line 1 to p. 217, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=217))
- Plan-selected projects get a fast path to a FERC siting permit ([p. 217, line 12 to p. 217, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=217))
- Six enumerated benefits; reliability first ([p. 213, line 19 to p. 213, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=213))

Neighboring regions must plan interregional lines together.

[p. 217, line 1 to p. 217, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=217)

Compliance with FERC's existing planning orders counts.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

FERC Orders 1000 and 1920 require regional planning by rule; interregional coordination is weak and there is no statutory requirement. DOE's triennial congestion study exists under section 216(a).

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 (sec. 402) created the same sections 224 and 225 but required only interregional plans. This bill also requires regional planning processes, deems FERC Order No. 1920 compliance sufficient for the regional piece, and exempts public power and small co-ops unless they opt in. It drops EPRA's 60-day FERC dispute resolution between regions and FERC's power to impose a plan when regions fail to file one; the only consequence left is a 6-month extension.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2104. Improvements relating to local transmission planning and development

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2104)

## Summary

Adds Federal Power Act section 226. One or more states may refer a utility to FERC for an investigation of its local transmission planning. FERC forms an investigative team with up to 3 state appointees. If the team finds the utility's process is not selecting the more efficient or cost-effective local projects, or is crowding out regional planning, FERC may order process changes, cut the utility's return on equity on local projects, remove the presumption of prudence, or fine the utility up to $5 million per imprudent facility, payable to the referring state.

## Key points

- States can trigger FERC investigations of local transmission spending ([p. 220, line 6 to p. 220, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=220))
- Remedies include lower return on equity and fines up to $5 million per facility ([p. 223, line 7 to p. 223, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=223))

## Selected statutory quotes

> A fine, payable to the referring State, of up to $5,000,000 for each local transmission facility

[p. 223, line 7 to p. 223, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=223)

Fines of up to $5 million per facility, paid to the state.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Local projects that a utility plans for itself get little federal or state review.

## Summary

Bans any federal right of first refusal for transmission facilities selected in a regional or interregional plan for cost allocation, overriding any FERC rule or order to the contrary.

## Key points

- Incumbent utilities get no federal first claim on regionally planned lines; competitive developers can bid ([p. 224, line 11 to p. 224, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=224))

## Selected statutory quotes

> a Federal right of first refusal is prohibited with respect to a transmission facility selected in a regional or interregional transmission plan for the purposes of cost allocation.

[p. 224, line 11 to p. 224, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=224)

The ban on a federal right of first refusal.

Order No. 1000 removed federal rights of first refusal; Order No. 1920 restored a conditional one for some upgrades. State right-of-first-refusal laws are untouched.

# Sec. 2106. Consolidated planning process

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2106)

## Summary

Requires FERC, within 18 months, to make each planning region file a consolidated interconnection and transmission planning process that looks 20 years ahead, publishes fuel-neutral planned interconnection locations with a fixed per-megawatt cost, and runs a cluster study with one decision point and nonrefundable security to deter speculative projects. Regions file within 2 years and update every 2 years.

## Key points

- Generation interconnection and transmission planned together ([p. 225, line 3 to p. 225, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=225))
- Published zonal per-megawatt interconnection prices ([p. 225, line 8 to p. 225, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=225))
- Nonrefundable deposits and withdrawal penalties for queue entrants ([p. 225, line 13 to p. 225, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=225))

## Selected statutory quotes

> routinely identifies and publishes resource and fuel-neutral planned interconnection locations for generating capacity and an upfront, fixed, zonal, per-megawatt cost for each planned interconnection location

[p. 225, line 8 to p. 225, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=225)

Published interconnection locations with a fixed per-megawatt cost.

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2107)

## Summary

Congress finds it is not just and reasonable to charge data center, AI and cryptocurrency loads less than the embedded and incremental cost of the transmission they need. FERC must revise its 1994 transmission pricing policy within 270 days, propose a rule 270 days after that, and finish within a further year.

New Federal Power Act section 228 covers data center loads of 20 megawatts or more. None of the incremental cost of serving them (generation, transmission, distribution) may be recovered from other customers. Recovery continues even if the data center leaves, and utilities must collect financial assurance before building upgrades.

States may charge these loads more than cost and credit the surplus to other ratepayers. They may run open seasons that award service by ratepayer benefit, whatever the queue order. They may require the load to bring new generation, require curtailable service, and treat data centers less favorably than other industrial customers. The section applies to loads interconnecting after enactment.

## Key points

- Data centers of 20 MW or more pay the full incremental cost of serving them ([p. 234, line 23 to p. 235, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=234))
- Costs follow the data center even after it exits ([p. 235, line 14 to p. 235, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=235))
- Up-front financial assurance before upgrades are built ([p. 235, line 23 to p. 236, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=235))
- States may auction grid access and require bring-your-own generation ([p. 236, line 23 to p. 237, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=236))
- Non-firm service gets a lower transmission price ([p. 230, line 9 to p. 230, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=230))
- Existing approved arrangements grandfathered ([p. 240, line 5 to p. 240, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=240))

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Cost allocation for large loads is set in individual state proceedings and FERC tariffs. FERC opened a large-load interconnection rulemaking in 2025. There is no federal floor.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Not in EPRA 2024; data center cost allocation became a central issue in 2025-2026.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2108. Dispatchable energy systems market access

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2108)

## Summary

Opens wholesale markets to aggregations of customer-sited batteries, fuel cells and generators that can respond within 15 minutes (5 kilowatts minimum per device, 100 kilowatts per aggregation). After 18 months, grid operator rules that block them are unjust and unreasonable. Grid operators file compliance tariffs within 180 days. Unless state law or the state regulator provides otherwise, distribution utilities in organized markets must interconnect these resources. They must also accept wholesale metering data.

A device paid by a state retail program cannot be paid twice for the same service; FERC orders disgorgement and can impose penalties of up to 3 times the amount for each day it was knowingly kept. The Energy Department runs a voluntary streamlined local permitting program for rooftop solar, batteries and vehicle chargers, with $20 million a year authorized for fiscal years 2026 through 2031.

## Key points

- Virtual power plants get statutory wholesale market access ([p. 243, line 20 to p. 243, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243))
- Device-level metering allowed; utilities cannot require their own equipment ([p. 241, line 16 to p. 241, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241))
- Double-payment ban, with penalties of up to 3 times the amount per day ([p. 250, line 16 to p. 250, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250))
- $20 million a year for streamlined local solar and storage permitting ([p. 259, line 22 to p. 259, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=259))

## Selected statutory quotes

> it shall not be just and reasonable within the meaning of sections 205 and 206 for any Transmission Organization to maintain rates, terms, or conditions of service that, by their terms and to the extent that such rates, terms, and conditions directly affect wholesale rates, prevent the participation of any qualifying BTM DES aggregation

[p. 243, line 15 to p. 243, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243)

Grid operators cannot bar aggregated customer-sited resources from wholesale markets.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

FERC Order No. 2222 (2020) requires aggregation access by rule; implementation has slipped to 2026 and beyond in several regions.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Not in EPRA 2024.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

## Full statutory text

Extracted from the official PDF; line cites mark paragraph starts. Consult the PDF for exact layout.

[p. 240, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=240) (indent level 1)

(a) DEFINITIONS.—Section 3 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 796) is amended by adding at the end the following:

[p. 240, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=240) (indent level 2)

“(30) QUALIFYING BEHIND-THE-METER DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SYSTEM FACILITY; QUALIFYING BTM DES FACILITY.—The term ‘qualifying behind-the-meter distributed energy system facility’ or ‘qualifying BTM DES facility’ means a facility that—

[p. 240, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=240) (indent level 3)

“(A) is an energy storage system (including a battery energy storage system), a fuel cell system, a generator, or other resource—

[p. 240, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=240) (indent level 4)

“(i) that can be brought online within 15 minutes of being called on for deployment; and

[p. 241, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 4)

“(ii) the output of which can be dispatched and adjusted at the signal of the system operator;

[p. 241, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 3)

“(B) is located behind the meter of a retail customer of a distribution utility (as defined in section 217(a));

[p. 241, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 3)

“(C) has a rated capacity of not less than 5 kilowatts; and

[p. 241, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 3)

“(D) maintains metering and telemetry capabilities that—

[p. 241, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 4)

“(i) are sufficient to dispatch the facility, account for withdrawals from and injections to the grid, and communicate all relevant operational data from the facility; and

[p. 241, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 4)

“(ii) are not required to include equipment owned or installed by the distribution utility (as so defined), and may include the use of device-level equipment, including inverters.

[p. 241, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=241) (indent level 2)

“(31) QUALIFYING BEHIND-THE-METER DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SYSTEM AGGREGATION; QUALIFYING BTM DES AGGREGATION.—The term ‘qualifying behind-the-meter distributed energy system aggregation’ or ‘qualifying BTM DES aggregation’ means an aggregation of 2 or more qualifying BTM DES facilities—

[p. 242, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 3)

“(A) with a combined capacity of not less than 100 kilowatts; and

[p. 242, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 3)

“(B) that maintains aggregation-level metering and telemetry capabilities sufficient to facilitate the dispatch and market settlement of the aggregation.”.

[p. 242, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 1)

(b) RULE OF CONSTRUCTION.—Section 201 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 824) is amended by adding at the end the following:

[p. 242, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 1)

“(h) QUALIFYING BTM DES FACILITIES AND AGGREGATIONS.— The designation of a facility as a qualifying BTM DES facility or an aggregation of 2 or more facilities as a qualifying BTM DES aggregation does not, of itself, subject any of the following to the jurisdiction of the Commission:

[p. 242, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 2)

“(1) The facility or aggregation.

[p. 242, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 2)

“(2) The retail electric service provided to or for the facility or aggregation.

[p. 242, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 2)

“(3) The distribution service on which the facility or aggregation relies.”.

[p. 242, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=242) (indent level 1)

(c) WHOLESALE MARKET ACCESS FOR QUALIFYING BTM DES AGGREGATIONS.—Part II of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 824 et seq.) (as amended by section 2107(b)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

[p. 243, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243) (indent level 0)

“SEC. 229. WHOLESALE MARKET ACCESS FOR QUALIFYING BTM DES AGGREGATIONS.

[p. 243, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243) (indent level 1)

“(a) DEFINITIONS.—In this section:

[p. 243, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243) (indent level 2)

“(1) COMMISSION.—The term ‘Commission’ means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

[p. 243, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243) (indent level 2)

“(2) DOUBLE COMPENSATION.—The term ‘double compensation’ means payment through or by both a wholesale market and a State-jurisdictional retail market or program for providing the same service during the same time interval.

[p. 243, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=243) (indent level 1)

“(b) JUST AND REASONABLE PRACTICES.—Effective on the date that is 18 months after the date of enactment of this section, it shall not be just and reasonable within the meaning of sections 205 and 206 for any Transmission Organization to maintain rates, terms, or conditions of service that, by their terms and to the extent that such rates, terms, and conditions directly affect wholesale rates, prevent the participation of any qualifying BTM DES aggregation in wholesale energy, capacity, or ancillary services markets administered by the Transmission Organization.

[p. 244, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 1)

“(c) PROHIBITED PRACTICES.—The following practices shall not be considered to be just and reasonable within the meaning of sections 205 and 206:

[p. 244, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 2)

“(1) Imposing metering, telemetry, or equipment requirements that are inconsistent with the definitions of the terms ‘qualifying BTM DES facility’ and ‘qualifying BTM DES aggregation’ in section 3.

[p. 244, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 2)

“(2) Requiring a qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation to participate in the energy market as a precondition to participating in the capacity market.

[p. 244, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 2)

“(3) Requiring the joint participation with any resource co-located with a Qualifying BTM DES facility as a condition for inclusion in a qualifying BTM DES aggregation.

[p. 244, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 2)

“(4) Any other practice otherwise described in subsection (b).

[p. 244, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 1)

“(d) COMPLIANCE FILINGS.—

[p. 244, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=244) (indent level 2)

“(1) TRANSMISSION ORGANIZATION FILINGS.— Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this section, each Transmission Organization that administers a wholesale market subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission shall file with the Commission proposed rates, terms, and conditions of service that comply with the requirements of this section.

[p. 245, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 2)

“(2) COMMISSION ACTION.—Not later than 180 days after the filing of a proposal under paragraph (1), the Commission shall—

[p. 245, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 3)

“(A) approve the proposal if the Commission determines that the proposal complies with this section; or

[p. 245, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 3)

“(B) require or impose such changes as the Commission determines to be just, reasonable, and in compliance with this section.

[p. 245, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 1)

“(e) COMPLAINTS.—

[p. 245, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—The Commission shall act on the merits of any complaint alleging noncompliance with this section not later than 180 days after the date on which the complaint is filed.

[p. 245, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 2)

“(2) CONSOLIDATION.—To maximize administrative efficiency, the Commission may consolidate and act upon related complaints with respect to a given Transmission Organization.

[p. 245, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 1)

“(f) DUAL PARTICIPATION; PROHIBITION ON DOUBLE COMPENSATION.—

[p. 245, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=245) (indent level 2)

“(1) PRESERVATION OF STATE PROGRAM ELIGIBILITY.— Participation by a qualifying BTM DES facility in a State-jurisdictional retail market or program shall not disqualify the qualifying BTM DES facility from participating in a wholesale market administered by a Transmission Organization, and nothing in this section requires a qualifying BTM DES facility to participate in any wholesale market.

[p. 246, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=246) (indent level 2)

“(2) PROHIBITION ON DOUBLE COMPENSATION.— No qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation shall receive double compensation.

[p. 246, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=246) (indent level 2)

“(3) QUALIFYING BTM DES RATE FILING.—

[p. 246, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=246) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this section, each Transmission Organization shall file with the Commission under section 205 revisions to its tariff establishing settlement, metering, and telemetry protocols that exclude from wholesale market settlement the quantity of energy, ancillary service, or capacity, evaluated on a service-by-service basis, for which a qualifying BTM DES facility has received or will receive compensation under a State-jurisdictional retail market or program, such that, for example, a BTM DES facility that has earned retail energy credit but not ancillary services or capacity credit may receive wholesale compensation for capacity and ancillary services without receiving any wholesale energy compensation.

[p. 247, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=247) (indent level 3)

“(B) ELECTRIC UTILITIES.—Each public utility that provides distribution service to a qualifying BTM DES facility shall provide to the applicable Transmission Organization and aggregator, in a form and on a schedule established by the Transmission Organization, the interval metering data and program-participation information necessary to implement subparagraph (A), subject to such protections for customer-specific information as the applicable State commission may require.

[p. 247, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=247) (indent level 3)

“(C) CERTIFICATION.—

[p. 247, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=247) (indent level 4)

“(i) IN GENERAL.—Each aggregator shall certify to the applicable Transmission Organization, on a schedule established by the Commission—

[p. 247, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=247) (indent level 5)

“(I) each State-jurisdictional retail market or program from which each qualifying BTM DES facility has received compensation; and

[p. 247, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=247) (indent level 5)

“(II) on the basis of final determinations made by the Commission arising from the proceedings initiated under subparagraph (A), that no qualifying BTM DES facility in its aggregation has retained double compensation during the certification period.

[p. 248, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=248) (indent level 4)

“(ii) TREATMENT.—A certification under this subparagraph shall constitute a statement made to the Commission for purposes of sections 316 and 316A.

[p. 248, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=248) (indent level 2)

“(4) COMPLAINT WITH RESPECT TO DOUBLE COMPENSATION.—

[p. 248, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=248) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—Any person, electric utility, State, municipality, or State commission aggrieved by alleged double compensation may file a complaint pursuant to section 206.

[p. 248, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=248) (indent level 3)

“(B) PROCEDURE.—In a proceeding initiated pursuant to a complaint under subparagraph (A), if a qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation that is the subject of the complaint meets the eligibility requirements of both a wholesale market and a State-jurisdictional program, the complainant in that proceeding shall—

[p. 248, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=248) (indent level 4)

“(i) bear the burden of proof before the Commission; and

[p. 249, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 4)

“(ii) demonstrate that—

[p. 249, line 2](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 5)

“(I) double compensation has in fact occurred or is imminent; and

[p. 249, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 5)

“(II) such double compensation could not be avoided through reasonable adjustments to—

[p. 249, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 6)

“(aa) wholesale market compensation received by the applicable qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation; or

[p. 249, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 6)

“(bb) the retail bill associated with the qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation, using metering and telemetry data that meets the requirements of the wholesale market.

[p. 249, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 3)

“(C) LIMITATION.—A complaint under subparagraph (A) shall be filed not later than 5 years after the date on which the alleged double compensation was received.

[p. 249, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=249) (indent level 2)

“(5) WHOLESALE MARKET COMPENSATION ADJUSTMENT.— If the Commission determines that double compensation could be avoided through an adjustment to a rate, term, or condition of service under the jurisdiction of the Commission pursuant to section 205, the Commission may initiate a proceeding consistent with section 206 to eliminate double compensation.

[p. 250, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250) (indent level 2)

“(6) DISGORGEMENT; PENALTIES.—

[p. 250, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250) (indent level 3)

“(A) DISGORGEMENT.—If the Commission finds that double compensation has occurred, the Commission shall order disgorgement of the full amount of the double compensation received.

[p. 250, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250) (indent level 3)

“(B) PENALTIES.—If the Commission determines that double compensation has been knowingly retained, the Commission may order penalties, which may include—

[p. 250, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250) (indent level 4)

“(i) monetary penalties of up to 3 times the amount of the double compensation received for each day that the double compensation was knowingly retained after the date of receipt, without regard to the limitations described in section 206(b); and

[p. 250, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=250) (indent level 4)

“(ii) suspension or termination of the participation of a qualifying BTM DES facility, qualifying BTM DES aggregation, or aggregator in a wholesale market administered by a Transmission Organization.

[p. 251, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 1)

“(g) ANNUAL REPORTING.—Each qualifying BTM DES facility and qualifying BTM DES aggregation participating in a wholesale market under this section shall submit to the Commission, not later than March 30 of each year, a public report that summarizes and quantifies all services provided by the qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation during the preceding calendar year to—

[p. 251, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 2)

“(1) wholesale markets subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission; and

[p. 251, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 2)

“(2) State-jurisdictional retail markets and programs within regions subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.”.

[p. 251, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 1)

(d) DISTRIBUTION UTILITY INTERCONNECTION AND NON-INTERFERENCE.—Part II of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 824 et seq.) (as amended by subsection (c)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

[p. 251, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 0)

“SEC. 230. DISTRIBUTION UTILITY OBLIGATIONS WITH RESPECT TO QUALIFYING BTM DES FACILITIES AND QUALIFYING BTM DES AGGREGATIONS.

[p. 251, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 1)

“(a) DEFINITIONS.—In this section:

[p. 251, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=251) (indent level 2)

“(1) COMMISSION.—The term ‘Commission’ means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

[p. 252, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 2)

“(2) DISTRIBUTION UTILITY; LOAD-SERVING ENTITY.—The terms ‘distribution utility’ and ‘load-serving entity’ have the meanings given those terms in section 217(a).

[p. 252, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 1)

“(b) INTERCONNECTION OBLIGATION.—

[p. 252, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—Except as otherwise provided by State law or by the State regulatory authority with jurisdiction over the distribution utility, any distribution utility located within the geographic footprint of an organized wholesale market administered by a Transmission Organization shall interconnect any behind-the-meter resource that is eligible to participate in that wholesale market, including any qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation, in a timely fashion and with rates, terms, and conditions of service that—

[p. 252, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 3)

“(A) allow the behind-the-meter resource to export energy to the grid, if applicable; and

[p. 252, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 3)

“(B) do not prevent, impede, or unreasonably condition the participation of the behind-the-meter resource in the wholesale market.

[p. 252, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=252) (indent level 2)

“(2) SAVINGS PROVISION.—Nothing in this subsection authorizes the Commission to prescribe the rates, terms, or conditions of distribution-level interconnection service.

[p. 253, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 1)

“(c) ACCEPTANCE OF WHOLESALE MARKET METERING DATA.—

[p. 253, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—Any distribution utility or load-serving entity providing retail electric service to a customer at whose premises a qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation is located shall accept the same metering and telemetry data used by the wholesale market for purposes of market participation by that qualifying BTM DES facility or qualifying BTM DES aggregation.

[p. 253, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 2)

“(2) REQUIREMENT.—The manner in which the data described in paragraph (1) is used to adjust the retail bill of a customer, including any adjustment to account for energy exported or withdrawn, shall be determined by the State regulatory authority having jurisdiction over retail rates.

[p. 253, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 1)

“(d) PROHIBITION ON INTERFERENCE.—

[p. 253, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—No distribution utility shall purposefully use its control over the distribution system or retail sales to prevent any behind-the-meter resource eligible to participate in a wholesale market subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission from participating in such wholesale market.

[p. 253, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=253) (indent level 2)

“(2) CERTAIN ACTIONS.—Nothing in this subsection limits a distribution utility from taking actions reasonably necessary to maintain the safety, reliability, or operations of the distribution system.

[p. 254, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 1)

“(e) COMMISSION ENFORCEMENT.—

[p. 254, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—The Commission shall have authority to enforce the provisions of this section, and any person may file with the Commission a complaint alleging a violation of this section.

[p. 254, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 2)

“(2) REQUIREMENT.—The Commission shall act on the merits of any complaint filed under paragraph (1) not later than 180 days after the date on which the complaint is filed.

[p. 254, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 1)

“(f) APPLICABILITY TO PUBLIC POWER AND CERTAIN COOPERATIVES.—Except to the extent that compliance is required under State law, the requirements of subsections (b), (c), and (d) shall be voluntary with respect to distribution utilities that are entities described in section 201(f).”.

[p. 254, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 1)

(e) ESTABLISHMENT OF PROGRAM TO FACILITATE VOLUNTARY STREAMLINED PROCESS FOR LOCAL PERMITTING OF QUALIFYING DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SYSTEMS.—

[p. 254, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 2)

(1) DEFINITIONS.—In this subsection:

[p. 254, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=254) (indent level 3)

(A) AUTHORITY HAVING JURISDICTION.— The term “authority having jurisdiction” means any State, county, local, or Tribal office or official with jurisdiction—

[p. 255, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=255) (indent level 4)

(i) to issue permits relating to qualifying distributed energy systems;

[p. 255, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=255) (indent level 4)

(ii) to conduct inspections to enforce the requirements of a relevant code or standard relating to qualifying distributed energy systems; or

[p. 255, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=255) (indent level 4)

(iii) to approve the installation of, or the equipment and materials used in the installation of, qualifying distributed energy systems.

[p. 255, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=255) (indent level 3)

(B) QUALIFYING DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SYSTEM.—The term “qualifying distributed energy system” means any equipment or materials installed in, on, or near a building or premises to support onsite or local energy use, including equipment or materials, the primary function of which is—

[p. 255, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=255) (indent level 4)

(i) to generate electricity from distributed renewable energy sources, including solar photovoltaic systems or similar solar energy technologies;

[p. 256, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=256) (indent level 4)

(ii) to store and discharge electricity from batteries with a capacity of at least 2 kilowatt hours;

# Sec. 2109. Advanced transmission technologies

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2109)

## Summary

Requires FERC to make public utilities use advanced transmission technologies, including best-available conductors, dynamic line rating, power flow control and topology optimization, in new and upgraded lines, with a presumption that the cost is prudent. FERC issues a rule within 1 year requiring recurring benefit-cost evaluations; when benefits exceed costs the utility must deploy on FERC's timeline or face a penalty such as a lower return on equity.

## Key points

- Mandatory use of grid-enhancing technologies when benefits exceed costs ([p. 263, line 16 to p. 263, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=263))
- Presumption of prudence for their cost ([p. 261, line 23 to p. 261, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=261))
- Return-on-equity penalty for not deploying ([p. 264, line 19 to p. 264, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=264))

## Selected statutory quotes

> the Commission shall require that public utilities use advanced transmission technologies, including best-available transmission conductors, when carrying out covered projects.

[p. 261, line 13 to p. 261, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=261)

Utilities must use advanced transmission technologies.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

FERC Order No. 1920 requires regions to consider four such technologies; nothing compels deployment.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 allowed advanced conductors in backstop projects but had no deployment mandate.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2111. Grid data access

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2111)

## Summary

Adds Federal Power Act section 232. Transmission providers must hold the data needed for interconnection and facilities studies and may demand it from any bulk-power system user, owner or operator, who must respond in 15 days in a usable format. Confidentiality rules can shape access but cannot be used to withhold data. Violations are treated as reliability matters. FERC and the Energy Department publish, within 1 year, a reference specification for fully automated interconnection studies.

## Key points

- 15-day deadline to hand over grid study data ([p. 268, line 21 to p. 268, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=268))
- Reference specification for fully automated interconnection studies ([p. 272, line 1 to p. 272, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=272))

## Selected statutory quotes

> may not be used to withhold grid data if access can be provided consistent with those requirements.

[p. 270, line 3 to p. 270, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=270)

Confidentiality rules cannot be used to withhold grid data.

(a) DEFINITION OF DATA CENTER ENTITY.—

[p. 279, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=279) (indent level 2)

(1) IN GENERAL.—In this section, the term “data center entity” means an end-user, or group of co-located end-users, the primary purpose of which is to house computing, networking, or data storage equipment used to process, store, or transmit digital data, including equipment used for—

[p. 279, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=279) (indent level 3)

[p. 279, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=279) (indent level 3)

(C) cryptocurrency mining or other distributed-ledger or digital-asset computation.

[p. 279, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=279) (indent level 2)

(2) EXCLUSION.—In this section, the term “data center entity” does not include computing or data storage equipment that is ancillary to a facility the primary purpose of which is commercial or industrial activity other than an activity described in paragraph (1).

[p. 279, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=279) (indent level 1)

(b) DATA COLLECTION.—Not later than 90 days before the first April 1 after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration shall revise Form 861 of the Energy Information Administration to include load from data center entities.

# Sec. 2201. Accelerating claims

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2201)

## Summary

A 150-day statute of limitations for any lawsuit challenging a federal agency's grant or denial of an authorization for an energy, carbon dioxide, mineral or wildfire fuel-reduction project, unless the underlying law sets a shorter one. Covered authorizations include leases, drilling permits, rights-of-way, mining plans, Endangered Species Act statements and permits, and forest restoration approvals. Agencies must publish the decision within 3 days. Courts must expedite the case, and a remand cannot give the agency more than 180 days unless the law requires longer. Agencies must tell the project sponsor about any suit within 30 days.

## Key points

- 150 days to sue over energy and mineral project decisions under any federal law ([p. 284, line 12 to p. 284, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=284))
- 180-day cap on agency action after a court remand ([p. 285, line 8 to p. 285, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=285))
- Covers oil and gas, mining, offshore, geothermal, rights-of-way and forest fuel-reduction projects ([p. 281, line 13 to p. 281, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=281))

## Selected statutory quotes

> a civil action arising under Federal law seeking judicial review of a final agency action granting or denying an authorization shall be barred unless the civil action is filed by the date that is 150 days after the date on which the grant or denial of the authorization is required to be made public

[p. 284, line 10 to p. 284, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=284)

The 150-day limit applies to claims under any federal law.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

The default limit for suits against the United States is 6 years; some statutes set shorter periods (60 days for Natural Gas Act orders, 2 years for FAST-41 covered projects).

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (sec. 101) nearly word for word: the 150-day limit, the 180-day remand cap and the 30-day notice to sponsors. This version adds leases, rights-of-way and easements to the definition and starts the clock when the decision is made public, which must happen within 3 days.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

The SPEED Act's 150-day limit applied to NEPA claims; this section reaches claims under any federal law for energy and mineral projects.

# Sec. 2211. Permitting compliance on non-Federal land

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. [Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2211)

## Summary

Removes the federal drilling permit requirement for oil and gas wells on non-federal surface land where the federal government owns less than half the minerals in the drilling unit, or where the wellbore only enters or passes through federal minerals. Lessees notify Interior of state permits. Interior cannot require bonds, mitigation or reclamation approval on that non-federal land. Royalties are unchanged; Indian lands are excluded.

## Key points

- No federal permit to drill for wells on private or state surface with a minority federal mineral interest ([p. 287, line 1 to p. 287, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=287))
- State permits govern; royalties still owed ([p. 289, line 1 to p. 289, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=289))

## Selected statutory quotes

> the Secretary of the Interior shall not require a permit to drill for an oil and gas lease under the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 181 et seq.) for an action occurring within an oil and gas drilling or spacing unit

[p. 286, line 21 to p. 286, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=286)

No federal drilling permit where the federal mineral share is under half.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

BLM requires an application for permit to drill whenever a well produces from a federal lease, wherever the surface is.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (sec. 203). EPRA's other onshore oil and gas changes, on lease nominations (sec. 201) and a 4-year drilling permit term (sec. 202), and its coal lease deadlines (sec. 204), are not in this bill.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2212. Rights-of-way across Indian land

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2212)

## Summary

Lets an Indian tribe grant rights-of-way across its own tribal land without Interior Department approval, if the grant follows a tribal regulation that Interior has approved. The tribal regulation must include an environmental review with public comment. Interior has 180 days to approve or disapprove, and its approval is not subject to NEPA, the National Historic Preservation Act or the Endangered Species Act.

## Key points

- Tribes can approve their own rights-of-way under an approved tribal regulation ([p. 291, line 8 to p. 291, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=291))
- Interior has 180 days to approve or disapprove a tribe's regulation ([p. 293, line 22 to p. 294, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=293))

## Selected statutory quotes

> an Indian tribe may grant a right-of-way over and across the Tribal land of the Indian tribe for any purpose.

[p. 291, line 8 to p. 291, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=291)

A tribe may grant a right-of-way across its own land.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Rights-of-way across tribal land need Interior approval under the 1948 Act and 25 CFR part 169. The HEARTH Act of 2012 already lets tribes approve their own surface leases under approved tribal regulations.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (sec. 205).

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2213. Accelerating renewable energy permitting

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2213)

## Summary

Interior or the Forest Service must tell an eligible-project applicant within 30 days whether its right-of-way application is complete. If an EIS is needed, the agency has 90 days after finding the application complete to issue a notice of intent. Within 30 days after a complete application is submitted, it must issue any required cost-recovery agreement and grant, deny or defer the application. Deferral requires notice of remaining steps and agency timelines.

Within 180 days, both departments must develop or adopt categorical exclusions for listed low-disturbance renewable activities, with extraordinary-circumstances exceptions. The list includes previously analyzed disturbances under 5 acres, certain repeat activities, small solar projects, surveys and meteorological towers. BLM must issue standard renewable review standards within 2 years.

## Key points

- 30-day completeness and decision clocks for renewable rights-of-way on public land ([p. 299, line 11 to p. 299, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=299))
- Categorical exclusions for small solar, met towers and geotechnical work within 180 days ([p. 301, line 22 to p. 301, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=301))
- Storage added to the definition of an eligible renewable project ([p. 303, line 22 to p. 303, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=303))

## Selected statutory quotes

> The installation, modification, operation, or removal of commercially available solar photovoltaic systems located on— (i) a building or other structure (such as a rooftop, parking lot, or facility, or mounted to signage, lighting, gates, or fences); or (ii) previously disturbed or developed land comprising less than 10 acres.

[p. 303, line 4 to p. 303, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=303)

Small solar installations are to be excluded from NEPA review.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

No statutory deadlines for renewable right-of-way applications; Interior's July 2025 policy sent wind and solar decisions to the Secretary's office for sign-off.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (secs. 206 and 207): the right-of-way clocks, the low-disturbance exclusions, storage as an eligible project, and the BLM review standards. EPRA's national goal of at least 50 gigawatts of renewable energy authorized on federal land by 2030 is not in this bill.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

## Summary

Directs Interior and Agriculture to adopt, within 180 days, categorical exclusions for placing power lines in approved corridors, for upgrades and reconductoring of existing lines in existing rights-of-way or on previously disturbed land, and for battery storage on previously disturbed land.

Battery storage on disturbed federal land gets a categorical exclusion.

# Sec. 2215. Hardrock mining mill sites

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2215)

## Summary

Lets a hardrock mine operator locate as many 5-acre mill sites on public land as are reasonably necessary for waste rock, tailings and other operations under an approved plan of operations, for a $400 annual fee per site. Mill sites convey no mineral rights and cannot be patented. Hardrock minerals on acquired federal lands become leasable. Mill site fees and those lease receipts go to a new Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund for cleanup.

## Key points

- A mine operator may locate as many 5-acre mill sites as its plan of operations needs ([p. 308, line 1 to p. 308, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=308))
- $400 per mill site per year, paid into an abandoned mine cleanup fund ([p. 311, line 12 to p. 311, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=311))

## Selected statutory quotes

> locate and include within the plan of operations as many mill site claims under this subsection as are reasonably necessary for its operations

[p. 308, line 7 to p. 308, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=308)

An operator may locate as many mill sites as its operations need.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Mill sites are capped at 5 acres each on non-mineral land. The Ninth Circuit held in 2022 (the Rosemont case) that waste rock cannot be stored on claims that lack a valuable mineral deposit.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (sec. 210, hardrock mining mill sites), including the cleanup fund.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act; the House passed a separate Mining Regulatory Clarity Act.

# Sec. 2221. Geothermal observation test projects

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. [Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2221)

## Summary

Requires a categorical exclusion within 1 year for geothermal observation test wells on existing leases that disturb no more than 10 acres, use no permanent roads, and finish within a year. Casual-use activities need only 30 days' notice and are not major federal actions.

## Key points

- Categorical exclusion for geothermal test wells up to 10 acres ([p. 324, line 17 to p. 324, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=324))

## Selected statutory quotes

> the Secretary concerned shall develop a categorical exclusion for geothermal observation test projects

[p. 324, line 18 to p. 324, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=324)

The exclusion for geothermal test wells.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

BLM adopted administrative geothermal exploration exclusions in 2024 and 2025; no statutory one.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 (sec. 208(a)) required a categorical exclusion for geothermal test activity under 10 acres within 180 days. This bill gives 1 year, defines the test projects in detail, and separately excludes them from NEPA as non-major actions (section 1102).

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2222. Geothermal royalties

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2222)

## Summary

Calculates the reduced early-years geothermal royalty per generating facility, starting from each facility's in-service date, so a second plant on an old lease gets its own 10-year lower-royalty period.

## Key points

- Royalty step-up clock runs per power plant, not per lease ([p. 328, line 22 to p. 328, line 25](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=328))

## Selected statutory quotes

> each year of the 10-year period following the in-service date of the geothermal electric generating facility

[p. 328, line 22 to p. 328, line 25](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=328)

The lower royalty period runs from each plant's in-service date.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

The lower royalty applies to the first 10 years of production under the lease.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Not in EPRA 2024 as reported.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2223. Geothermal leasing reform

## Summary

Requires geothermal lease sales every year instead of every 2 years, with a replacement sale in the same year if one is cancelled, and sets 30-day completeness and 30-day decision deadlines for geothermal drilling permits.

## Key points

- Annual geothermal lease sales ([p. 329, line 18 to p. 329, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=329))
- 30-day drilling permit clocks ([p. 330, line 3 to p. 330, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=330))

## Selected statutory quotes

> If a lease sale under paragraph (1) for a year is cancelled or delayed, the Secretary shall conduct a replacement sale during the same year.

[p. 329, line 18 to p. 329, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=329)

A cancelled lease sale must be replaced the same year.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Lease sales at least every 2 years; no permit deadlines.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Carried over from EPRA 2024 (sec. 208(b) and (c)), with the completeness check lengthened from 10 to 30 days and a hard 10-day deadline added for deferred decisions.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2224. Geothermal ombudsman and permitting task force

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2224)

## Summary

Creates a Geothermal Ombudsman and a Geothermal Permitting Task Force inside BLM within 60 days to resolve disputes between field offices and applicants, move staff to offices with backlogs, and pay retention allowances of up to 25 percent of basic pay.

## Key points

- BLM geothermal ombudsman and strike team ([p. 333, line 5 to p. 333, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=333))

## Selected statutory quotes

> provide dispute resolution services for disputes between the individual field, district, and State offices of the Bureau and applicants for geothermal authorizations

[p. 333, line 18 to p. 333, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=333)

The ombudsman resolves disputes between BLM offices and applicants.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

New.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 (sec. 208(g)) created the Geothermal Ombudsman. The task force, staff reassignments and retention allowances are new.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2225. No Federal permit required for geothermal activities on certain land

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2225)

## Summary

No federal drilling permit for geothermal exploration and production on non-federal surface where the United States owns less than 50 percent of the subsurface geothermal estate, if the operator files its state permit with Interior. Indian lands are excluded; royalties are unchanged.

## Key points

- State permits suffice for geothermal wells with a minority federal interest ([p. 338, line 20 to p. 338, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=338))

## Selected statutory quotes

> The Secretary shall not require an operator to obtain a Federal drilling permit for geothermal exploration and production activities conducted on a non-Federal surface estate

[p. 338, line 20 to p. 338, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=338)

No federal drilling permit on non-federal surface with a minority federal interest.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

A federal permit is required.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Parallel to EPRA 2024's oil and gas provision; the geothermal version is new.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

Applications are decided within 60 days even while a lawsuit is pending.

# Sec. 2229. NEPA Review

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2229)

## Summary

Rewrites section 390 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005. The five listed oil and gas activities (small surface disturbances, drilling at an existing pad, drilling in a developed field, pipelines in approved corridors, minor maintenance) are no longer treated through categorical exclusions; they are declared not to be major federal actions at all, and geothermal is added. The corridor look-back for pipelines goes from 5 to 10 years, and geothermal gets a new item for power lines up to 20 miles in an approved corridor. Drilling permits for these activities carry no NEPA requirements.

## Key points

- Section 390 oil, gas and now geothermal activities are outside NEPA entirely ([p. 349, line 9 to p. 349, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=349))
- Drilling permits for those activities 'shall not have any requirements' under NEPA ([p. 351, line 6 to p. 351, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=351))

## Selected statutory quotes

> shall not be considered a major Federal action under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.) if the activity is conducted pursuant to the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 181 et seq.) or the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 (30 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) for the purpose of exploration or development of oil, gas, or geothermal resources.

[p. 349, line 9 to p. 349, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=349)

Routine oil, gas and geothermal activities are declared not to be major federal actions.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Section 390 creates a rebuttable presumption that a categorical exclusion applies to five oil and gas activities; extraordinary circumstances review has been contested.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

EPRA 2024 (sec. 208(f)) extended the section 390 categorical exclusions to geothermal. Declaring the activities not major federal actions, and stripping NEPA from the drilling permits, goes further and applies to oil and gas as well.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.
