## Summary

Bars FERC from requiring license amendments for routine hydropower maintenance, repair or replacement, or for temporary operating variances caused by events outside the licensee's control. FERC must propose a rule within 90 days and finish within a further 180 days defining which alterations are substantial enough to need approval. Dam safety authority is preserved.

## Key points

- No FERC approval needed for routine hydropower maintenance ([p. 355, line 8 to p. 355, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=355))

## Selected statutory quotes

> The Commission shall not require approval or an amendment to a project license for any routine maintenance, repair, or replacement of any portion of a project works

[p. 355, line 8 to p. 355, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=355)

Routine dam maintenance no longer needs FERC sign-off.

# Sec. 2251. Offshore energy

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2251)

## Summary

Amends the offshore renewable energy section of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act. Interior's duty changes from 'prevention of interference with reasonable uses' of the ocean to 'prevention of unreasonable interference with other uses'. Interior may grant rights-of-way for electric transmission through national marine sanctuaries, with sanctuary permits lasting as long as the right-of-way. The Inflation Reduction Act's link between offshore wind leasing and oil and gas lease sales is preserved.

## Key points

- Offshore wind standard changes to 'unreasonable interference' ([p. 363, line 16 to p. 363, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=363))
- Transmission cables allowed through marine sanctuaries ([p. 364, line 7 to p. 364, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=364))

## Selected statutory quotes

> by striking “prevention of interference with reasonable uses” and inserting “prevention of unreasonable interference with other uses”

[p. 363, line 15 to p. 363, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=363)

The offshore wind test becomes 'unreasonable interference' with other uses.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Section 8(p)(4)(I) requires prevention of interference with reasonable uses of the exclusive economic zone, the high seas and the territorial seas.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

The three Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act amendments come from EPRA 2024 (sec. 302(d)), with one change: sanctuary rights-of-way are no longer limited to electricity from renewable energy. EPRA's mandates do not appear here: one offshore oil and gas lease sale and one offshore wind lease sale a year from 2025 to 2029, 400,000 acres of wind leasing a year, and a 30-gigawatt offshore wind goal.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

# Sec. 2252. Offshore energy transmission

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

## Summary

Directs Interior and Energy to identify preferred routes for offshore transmission cables within 2 years and review them every 3 years, makes Interior the lead agency for offshore transmission permitting, requires a final rule within 2 years, and lets Interior issue offshore transmission rights-of-way competitively or noncompetitively.

## Key points

- Interior is lead agency; rights-of-way can be noncompetitive ([p. 369, line 8 to p. 369, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=369))

## Selected statutory quotes

> shall identify preferred routes on the outer Continental Shelf for transmission cables and sub-seabed infrastructure

Interior and Energy must identify preferred offshore cable routes.

# Sec. 2301. Historic preservation

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

Saved AI review: 401 supported, 12 flagged, 127 unchecked of 540 statements; checked 2026-10-01; stale: true. Coverage excludes current-law comparison cells and some research paraphrases. Read data/core.json checks for link and quote results and their dates. A stale review does not verify the current wording.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2301)

## Summary

Rewrites section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. An 'adverse effect' must be reasonably foreseeable and must directly alter a historic property. Temporary alterations are excluded. Visual, atmospheric and audible effects are excluded unless they directly and significantly diminish the property. An 'undertaking' excludes projects whose only federal tie is a loan, guarantee or grant, the non-federal parts of a project, minor repairs, permit renewals and post-approval operations.

The process gets deadlines: 30 days to decide whether a project is an undertaking, 60 days for the agency's report, 90 days for a determination, then 60 days of consultation, 45 days for Advisory Council comments and 30 days for a final decision. Consultation must be finished by the time the NEPA document is completed, unless the Secretary grants an extension for extraordinary circumstances. State and tribal preservation officers who do not respond in 30 days are passed over, and the agency may decide in its sole discretion that other considerations outweigh preservation.

Courts give substantial deference and may only remand without vacatur or injunction; a preliminary injunction is available only for a likely violation of another law. Claims go to the courts of appeals, within 150 days, from parties who commented and suffered direct harm. A suit over a missed consultation deadline goes to a court where the project is located. Non-signatories cannot challenge programmatic agreements. State and tribal programs are evaluated every 2 years and lose grants if they miss consultation timelines.

## Key points

- Adverse effect limited to direct physical alteration; visual and noise effects mostly excluded ([p. 380, line 5 to p. 380, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380))
- Loans and grants alone no longer trigger section 106 ([p. 383, line 22 to p. 383, line 24](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383))
- End-to-end deadlines; silence from a preservation officer after 30 days lets the agency proceed ([p. 400, line 19 to p. 400, line 21](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=400))
- Agency may find other considerations outweigh preservation 'in the sole discretion' of the official ([p. 391, line 13 to p. 391, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=391))
- 150-day limit, court of appeals jurisdiction, remand without vacatur ([p. 408, line 23 to p. 408, line 25](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=408))
- Later National Register listings do not reopen a review ([p. 413, line 14 to p. 413, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=413))

## Selected statutory quotes

> any visual, atmospheric, or audible element, unless the visual, atmospheric, or audible element would have a direct impact on a historic property that would significantly diminish the eligible characteristics of the historic property

[p. 380, line 13 to p. 380, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380)

Visual, atmospheric and audible effects mostly no longer count as adverse.

> in the sole discretion of the Federal official and as otherwise allowed by law, other considerations outweigh the consideration of historic preservation as to any or all adverse effects of the undertaking

[p. 393, line 4 to p. 393, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=393)

The agency may decide that other considerations outweigh preservation.

> the only remedy the court may order is to remand, without vacatur or issuance of an injunction, the applicable agency action to the Federal agency

[p. 406, line 25 to p. 407, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=406)

Remand is the only remedy, as in the NEPA title.

## Comparison notes

- [SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), engrossed in House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm)
- [Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (S. 4753), reported in Senate](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm)

### Current law

Section 106 is one sentence requiring agencies to 'take into account' effects on historic properties; the process lives in Advisory Council regulations (36 CFR part 800) with no statutory deadlines, a broad definition of adverse effect that includes visual and audible intrusions, and ordinary APA review.

### EPRA 2024 (reported S. 4753)

Not in EPRA 2024. This is the first major permitting bill to rewrite section 106.

### SPEED Act (House-passed H.R. 4776)

Not in the SPEED Act.

[p. 380, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 4)

“(i) is reasonably foreseeable; and

[p. 380, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 4)

“(ii) directly alters the characteristics of a historic property in a manner that would diminish the integrity of the location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, or association of the historic property.

[p. 380, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 3)

“(B) EXCLUSIONS.—The term ‘adverse effect of the undertaking’ does not include—

[p. 380, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 4)

“(i) any visual, atmospheric, or audible element, unless the visual, atmospheric, or audible element would have a direct impact on a historic property that would significantly diminish the eligible characteristics of the historic property;

[p. 380, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 4)

“(ii) any temporary alteration to a historic property that is limited to the time it takes to complete an undertaking; or

[p. 380, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=380) (indent level 4)

“(iii) any effect on a portion of the historic property other than an adverse effect to the character-defining features, such as contributing elements, cultural-use locations, or access points, that significantly contribute to the qualification of the property for inclusion on the National Register.

[p. 381, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 2)

“(2) AREA OF POTENTIAL EFFECTS.—

[p. 381, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—The term ‘area of potential effects’ means the area within which an undertaking may cause an effect described in paragraph (1)(A).

[p. 381, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 3)

“(B) EXCLUSION.—The term ‘area of potential effects’ does not include any geographic area affected solely by a portion of a project, activity, or program that is not subject to Federal control or responsibility.

[p. 381, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 2)

“(3) MADE PUBLIC.—The term ‘made public’, with respect to a final agency action, means that the final agency action is published in a single location on the primary website of the applicable Federal agency with—

[p. 381, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 3)

“(A) hyperlinks to the final agency action prominently displayed on the website; and

[p. 381, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 3)

“(B) the date of initial publication of the final agency action displayed and maintained on the website.

[p. 381, line 25](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=381) (indent level 2)

“(4) REASONABLY FORESEEABLE.—

[p. 382, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—The term ‘reasonably foreseeable’, with respect to an adverse effect of the undertaking, means an effect of the undertaking that shares a reasonably close causal relationship to, and is proximately caused by, the undertaking being considered.

[p. 382, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 3)

“(B) EXCLUSIONS.—The term ‘reasonably foreseeable’, with respect to an adverse effect of the undertaking, does not include—

[p. 382, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 4)

“(i) any adverse effect of the undertaking that is speculative or attenuated from the undertaking; or

[p. 382, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 4)

“(ii) any adverse effect of the undertaking relating to an unrelated prior, separate existing, or potential future undertaking.

[p. 382, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 2)

“(5) STATE HISTORIC PRESERVATION OFFICER.— The term ‘State Historic Preservation Officer’ means—

[p. 382, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 3)

“(A) the official designated and appointed pursuant to section 302301(1) to administer the State Historic Preservation Program; or

[p. 382, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=382) (indent level 3)

“(B) a representative designated to act for the official described in subparagraph (A).

[p. 383, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 2)

“(6) TRIBAL HISTORIC PRESERVATION OFFICER.— The term ‘Tribal Historic Preservation Officer’ means the Tribal official designated pursuant to section 302702(2) who has assumed the duties of the State Historic Preservation Officer for purposes of compliance with subsection (b) within the boundaries of the applicable tribal land.

[p. 383, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 2)

“(7) UNDERTAKING.—

[p. 383, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—The term ‘undertaking’ means a project, activity, or program that—

[p. 383, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 4)

“(i) requires a Federal permit, license, or approval; and

[p. 383, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 4)

“(ii) is subject to substantial Federal control and responsibility.

[p. 383, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 3)

“(B) EXCLUSION.—The term ‘undertaking’ does not include—

[p. 383, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 4)

“(i) any portion of a project, activity, or program over which a Federal agency does not exercise substantial control or responsibility over the outcome;

[p. 383, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=383) (indent level 4)

“(ii) a project, activity, or program for which the only Federal involvement is a loan, loan guarantee, grant (including a capitalization grant), cost-share award, or other form of financial assistance that is not for the primary purpose of historic preservation;

[p. 384, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 4)

“(iii) a project, activity, or program that consists of minor restoration, rehabilitation, repair, maintenance, stabilization, hazardous material remediation, structure hardening, provision of handicapped access, or other similar minor projects that do not diminish the integrity of a historic property;

[p. 384, line 12](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 4)

“(iv) a project, activity, or program that is a survey or work completed to conduct consultations;

[p. 384, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 4)

“(v) a project, activity, or program that—

[p. 384, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 5)

“(I) is any alteration to a historic property that is necessary for public safety; and

[p. 384, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 5)

“(II) does not diminish the integrity of the historic property;

[p. 384, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=384) (indent level 4)

“(vi) an activity or decision that is non-discretionary and made in accordance with the statutory authority of the Federal agency;

[p. 385, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=385) (indent level 4)

“(vii) any—

[p. 385, line 2](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=385) (indent level 5)

“(I) renewal of a special use permit on the expiration of the special use permit if no substantive changes are made from the original special use permit; or

[p. 385, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=385) (indent level 5)

“(II) transfer of ownership of a special use permit;

[p. 385, line 9](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=385) (indent level 4)

“(viii) the implementation of, or any act or omission under, a memorandum of agreement, programmatic agreement, or other instrument executed in connection with compliance with this section, after the date on which a determination has been made under subsection (c); or

[p. 385, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=385) (indent level 4)

“(ix) the continuation, operation, maintenance, or post-approval implementation of a project, activity, or program after the determination has been made under subsection (c), except that a subsequent discrete decision of a Federal agency to amend or materially modify a determination made under subsection (c) is itself an undertaking, to the extent provided in this section.”; and

[p. 386, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 2)

(4) by adding at the end the following:

“(c) CONSULTATION.—

[p. 386, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 2)

“(1) IN GENERAL.—The responsibilities of a Federal agency under this section shall be limited to historic properties within the area of potential effects identified by the Federal agency.

[p. 386, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 2)

“(2) INITIATION AND REPORT.—

[p. 386, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—Not later than 30 days after the date of receipt of a request for review of a proposed project, activity, or program under this section, the applicable Federal official shall determine whether the proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking subject to the requirements of this section.

[p. 386, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 3)

“(B) ESTABLISHMENT OF AREA OF POTENTIAL EFFECTS AND IDENTIFICATION AND DETERMINATION OF HISTORIC PROPERTIES.—

[p. 386, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=386) (indent level 4)

“(i) IN GENERAL.—If the applicable Federal official determines under subparagraph (A) that the proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking, the applicable Federal official shall establish the area of potential effects for the undertaking.

[p. 387, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=387) (indent level 4)

“(ii) IDENTIFICATION OF HISTORIC PROPERTIES.—The applicable Federal official shall identify and determine any historic properties within the area of potential effects.

[p. 387, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=387) (indent level 4)

“(iii) CONSULTATION.—For purposes of establishing the area of potential effects for the undertaking and identifying and determining any historic properties under clauses (i) and (ii), respectively, the applicable Federal official may consult with any applicable State Historic Preservation Officers, Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, Indian tribes, or Native Hawaiian organizations, local governments, and project, activity, or program applicants.

[p. 387, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=387) (indent level 4)

“(iv) INCORPORATION OF INFORMATION.— Upon a determination made under subparagraph (A), before establishing the area of potential effects under clause (i) or identifying and determining historic properties under clause (ii), the applicable Federal official shall seek, discuss, as appropriate, and incorporate, as applicable, information from each applicable State Historic Preservation Officer, Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, Indian tribe, or Native Hawaiian organization, local government, and project, activity, or program applicant, if the information is communicated to the applicable Federal official not later than 30 days after the date on which the Federal official submits a request for such information.

[p. 388, line 10](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=388) (indent level 3)

“(C) PROGRAM ALTERNATIVE.—If the applicable Federal official determines under subparagraph (A) that the proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking that is governed by a program alternative authorized under section 800.14 of title 36, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations), including an alternate procedure, programmatic agreement, exempted category, standard treatment, or program comment, the applicable Federal official may follow the applicable program alternative with respect to the undertaking.

[p. 388, line 22](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=388) (indent level 3)

“(D) DETERMINATION OF EFFECTS.—

[p. 388, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=388) (indent level 4)

“(i) IN GENERAL.—If the applicable Federal official determines that a proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking under subparagraph (A), the applicable Federal official shall determine whether there are any adverse effects of the undertaking within the area of potential effects.

[p. 389, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=389) (indent level 4)

“(ii) NO ADVERSE EFFECTS.—The applicable Federal official shall have no further obligations under this section if the applicable Federal official determines under clause (i) that—

[p. 389, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=389) (indent level 5)

“(I) the proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking for which there are no adverse effects of the undertaking;

[p. 389, line 15](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=389) (indent level 5)

“(II) the undertaking does not have the potential to cause adverse effects of the undertaking; or

[p. 389, line 18](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=389) (indent level 5)

“(III) historic properties are not present.

[p. 389, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=389) (indent level 4)

“(iii) REPORT.—If the applicable Federal official determines under subparagraph (A) that the proposed project, activity, or program is an undertaking, for which there will be adverse effects of the undertaking, as determined under clause (i), not later than 60 days after the date of the determination under subparagraph (A), the applicable Federal official shall complete and submit for review to the applicable State Historic Preservation Officer, Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, Indian tribe, Native Hawaiian organization, local government, and project, activity, or program applicant under this division a report that—

[p. 390, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=390) (indent level 5)

“(I) identifies whether historic properties are present within the area of potential effects; and

[p. 390, line 14](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=390) (indent level 5)

“(II) if historic properties are present within the area of potential effects—

[p. 390, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=390) (indent level 6)

“(aa) identifies the area of potential effects for the undertaking;

[p. 390, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=390) (indent level 6)

“(bb) identifies the historic properties within the area of potential effects;

[p. 390, line 23](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=390) (indent level 6)

“(cc) considers only the portion of the property within the area of potential effects;

[p. 391, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=391) (indent level 6)

“(dd) documents the adverse effects of the undertaking;

[p. 391, line 3](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=391) (indent level 6)

“(ee) identifies prudent and feasible measures within the area of potential effects to avoid, minimize, or mitigate the adverse effects of the undertaking;

[p. 391, line 8](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=391) (indent level 6)

“(ff) identifies and explains any case in which, as applicable, the applicable Federal official has decided not to require such prudent and feasible measures because, in the sole discretion of the applicable Federal official and as otherwise allowed by law, other considerations outweigh the consideration of historic preservation as to any or all adverse effects of the undertaking; and

[p. 391, line 20](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=391) (indent level 6)

“(gg) does not identify measures described in item (ee) that are not prudent or would occur outside the area of potential effects, unless the project, activity, or program applicant has submitted a written request for alternative mitigation measures.

“(3) DETERMINATION.—

[p. 392, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=392) (indent level 3)

“(A) IN GENERAL.—Not later than 90 days after the date of submission of a report under paragraph (2)(D)(iii), unless a shorter timeline is agreed to by the State Historic Preservation Officer or Tribal Historic Preservation Officer and each applicable Indian tribe, Native Hawaiian organization, and local government, the applicable Federal official, in consultation with the applicable State Historic Preservation Officer and Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, Indian tribe, Native Hawaiian organization, and local government under this division, shall—

[p. 392, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=392) (indent level 4)

“(i) determine, based on the report, that—

[p. 392, line 19](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=392) (indent level 5)

“(I)(aa) the adverse effects of the undertaking would not so diminish the integrity of the historic property to the extent that the historic property would be made ineligible for listing on the National Register; and

[p. 393, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=393) (indent level 6)

“(bb) the obligations of the Federal official under this section shall be satisfied; or

“(bb) the obligations of the Federal official under this section shall be satisfied; or

“(B) NO AGREEMENT.—

“(A) IN GENERAL.—If more than 1 Federal agency has jurisdiction over a project, activity, or program that is determined to be an undertaking, the 1 or more applicable Federal agencies shall designate a lead Federal agency to comply with the requirements of this subsection.

[p. 396, line 5](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=396) (indent level 3)

“(5) TIMELINES FOR CONSULTATION.—

[p. 397, line 16](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=397) (indent level 3)

“(A) INITIATION.—If a project, activity, or program requires the preparation of an environmental document under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.), any consultation with respect to the project, activity, or program required for purposes of this subsection shall initiate not later than the date of initiation of the environmental review.

[p. 397, line 25](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=397) (indent level 3)

“(B) COMPLETION.—

[p. 398, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=398) (indent level 4)

“(i) IN GENERAL.—The consultation process initiated under subparagraph (A) shall be completed not later than the date on which the applicable environmental document under section 107(g) of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4336a(g)) is completed with respect to the undertaking, unless the Secretary approves an extension of the deadline due to extraordinary circumstances beyond the control, and not due to any actions, of the consulting parties.

[p. 398, line 13](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=398) (indent level 4)

“(ii) FAILURE TO COMPLETE BY DEADLINE.—If the consultation process initiated under subparagraph (A) is not complete by the later of the deadline established under clause (i) or the date extended under that clause, the consultation requirement for purposes of this subsection, each State Historic Preservation Officer, Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, and employee within Senior Executive Service (as defined in section 2101a of title 5) that has supervisory authority over personnel in a relevant agency that has a substantive role or responsibility in the consultation, shall spend not less than 50 percent of the workweek, as determined pursuant to title 5 or other applicable law, to remedy the failure.

[p. 399, line 6](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=399) (indent level 4)

“(iii) CAUSES OF ACTION.—

[p. 399, line 7](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=399) (indent level 5)

“(I) RIGHT TO PETITION.—A project, activity, or program applicant may obtain judicial review of the compliance by a Federal agency with the deadline established under clause (i) by filing a complaint with a court of competent jurisdiction in which a substantial part of the applicable proposed project, activity, or program is situated.

[p. 399, line 17](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=399) (indent level 5)

“(II) REMEDY.—If a court of competent jurisdiction under this clause finds that a Federal agency has failed to act in accordance with this subsection, the court shall provide injunctive relief, as appropriate, to give effect to this subsection and retain jurisdiction to ensure compliance with any such relief.

[p. 400, line 1](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=400) (indent level 5)

“(III) EXPEDITED PROCEDURES; TIME TO DECIDE.—The reviewing court under this clause shall—

[p. 400, line 4](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=400) (indent level 6)

“(aa) establish an expedited schedule for briefing and disposition; and

# Sec. 2302. Funding for the Historic Preservation Fund; use and availability; grants for Tribal Historic Preservation officers; additional funding

BAAJA draft released September 30, 2026. AI-assisted analysis; proposed changes.

[Official PDF](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/5/c/5c5f5935-b224-48e7-abea-e60c30e7a4cf/7935BF3C85967B6F56F6F4858FD3221B7E0AEB02D04BE391CAFBD1B884CE3DC5.bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-text.pdf) · [Browser section](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/#/bill/sec/2302)

## Summary

Authorizes $200 million a year for deposit in the Historic Preservation Fund for fiscal years 2027 through 2036. Deposits become available the next fiscal year without a further appropriation. Creates a $20 million-a-year grant program (fiscal years 2027 through 2030) for tribal historic preservation officers to build online databases of records and of properties of traditional religious or cultural importance, with protections against disclosing sensitive site locations.

## Key points

- $200 million a year for the Historic Preservation Fund through 2036 ([p. 414, line 10 to p. 414, line 11](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=414))
- $20 million a year for tribal preservation databases ([p. 417, line 1 to p. 417, line 2](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/bill.pdf#page=417))
