- epra: No change.
- speed: Adds that NEPA is 'a purely procedural statute' that 'does not mandate particular results'.
  Source: [Sec. 2(a)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Adds that NEPA prescribes a procedure that ends in an informational document, and that nothing in it mandates a particular outcome.
  Bill: [1101](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1101.md)
### Actions outside NEPA

- current: Seven exclusions since 2023, including projects with minimal federal funding and loans where the agency lacks sufficient control.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336e(10)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336e)
- epra: No change.
- speed: Adds grants and cost-share awards, Farm Service Agency loans, and actions another agency already reviewed. Federal money alone cannot make an action major.
  Source: [Sec. 2(f)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Fourteen exclusions. Adds loan-only projects, routine actions up to $10 million, lifeline infrastructure repair, geothermal test wells, in-corridor grid and gas pipeline work, previously reviewed actions, and Corps projects up to a $50 million federal share.
  Bill: [1102](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1102.md)
  Bill: [2102](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2102.md)
### Effects an agency must study

- current: 'Reasonably foreseeable' effects. The Supreme Court held in 2025 that agencies need not study separate upstream or downstream projects.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4332(2)(C); Seven County v. Eagle County](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4332)
- epra: No change.
- speed: Only effects proximately caused by the project itself. Speculative effects and effects of separate projects are excluded.
  Source: [Sec. 2(b), 2(f)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: No statutory limit on scope. Courts must give agencies substantial deference on the scope and contents of the document.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Ways to skip a full review

- current: An agency's own categorical exclusions, or another agency's after consultation and public notice.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336(a), 4336c](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336)
- epra: Orders new categorical exclusions for renewable, geothermal and grid work on federal land.
  Source: [Secs. 206, 208, 209](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20206.%20ACCELERATING%20RENEWABLE%20ENERGY%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Adds exclusions enacted by Congress. Another statute or a state or tribal review can stand in for NEPA. A lead agency's finding that no document is needed binds other agencies.
  Source: [Sec. 2(b), 2(e)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Same substitutes and the same binding rule, plus combining several exclusions on one project and a public CEQ register of every exclusion.
  Bill: [1105](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1105.md)
  Bill: [1108](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1108.md)
### Review deadlines

- current: EIS in 2 years and EA in 1 year, counted from the earliest of the agency's determination, a complete application, or the notice of intent. Page limits of 150 and 75.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336a(e), (g)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336a)
- epra: No change.
- speed: Keeps the 2023 deadlines. Adds 60 days to judge an application complete and 60 days to pick the level of review.
  Source: [Sec. 2(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Same 2-year and 1-year deadlines and page limits, counted from the earlier of the agency's determination or a complete application. Same two 60-day front-end clocks.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
  Bill: [1109](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1109.md)
### Decisions after the review

- current: No general deadline for the record of decision or for other agencies' permits.
- epra: Project-specific clocks, such as 30 days to decide a renewable right-of-way once reviews are done.
  Source: [Sec. 206](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20206.%20ACCELERATING%20RENEWABLE%20ENERGY%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Final agency action within 30 days of the finished EIS or EA.
  Source: [Sec. 2(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Finding of no significant impact within 7 days of an EA. Record of decision within 45 days of an EIS. All federal permits within 90 days, or 120 days for agencies outside the review.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
### New science during a review

- current: Agencies need not do new research unless it is essential and the cost and time are reasonable.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336(b)(3)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336)
- epra: No change.
- speed: No new research after an application arrives. No duty to consider research published after the earlier of the application or the notice of intent.
  Source: [Sec. 2(b), 2(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: No duty to consider research published after the notice of intent, and no delay to wait for it.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
### Alternatives

- current: A reasonable range of alternatives that are feasible and meet the purpose and need.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4332(2)(C)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4332)
- epra: No change.
- speed: The statement of purpose and need must meet the applicant's goals.
  Source: [Sec. 2(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: The lead agency must drop any alternative that misses the purpose and need or the non-federal sponsor's goals. The no-action alternative stays.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
### Missed deadlines

- current: A sponsor may petition a court, which can order the agency to act within 90 days.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336a(g)(3)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336a)
- epra: No change.
- speed: Extensions only with the applicant's approval. A sponsor that approved one cannot petition a court unless the agency misses the new deadline.
  Source: [Sec. 2(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Once a deadline is 60 days overdue the agency head may not travel more than 25 miles from the duty station. Senior staff must spend half the workweek on the review when the agency has defied a CEQ dispute order. Courts must rule on a sponsor's petition within 120 days and can order a decision in 60.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
### CEQ's role

- current: Designates a lead agency within 40 days when agencies disagree. CEQ removed its own NEPA regulations in 2025 and 2026.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336a(a)(5)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336a)
- epra: No change.
- speed: No structural change.
- senate: The Chairman names lead agencies in 21 days and settles interagency disputes by final orders no court can review. CEQ runs a public permitting tracker, an ePermit portal targeted for December 1, 2028, and a $20 million-a-year improvement fund.
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)
  Bill: [1121](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1121.md)
  Bill: [1132](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1132.md)
  Bill: [1133](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1133.md)
### Programmatic reviews

- current: Reliable for 5 years without reevaluation.
  Source: [42 U.S.C. 4336b](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/4336b)
- epra: No change.
- speed: 10 years. Agencies may also reuse an earlier review of a substantially similar action.
  Source: [Sec. 2(d)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: 10 years.
  Bill: [1107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1107.md)
### Time limit for a NEPA suit

- current: 6 years by default, 2 years for FAST-41 projects, 150 days for highways and transit.
  Source: [28 U.S.C. 2401(a); 42 U.S.C. 4370m-6; 23 U.S.C. 139(l)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/2401)
- epra: 150 days for energy and mineral project decisions.
  Source: [Sec. 101](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20101.%20ACCELERATING%20CLAIMS)
- speed: 150 days.
  Source: [Sec. 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%203.%20JUDICIAL%20REVIEW)
- senate: 150 days.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Who can sue

- current: Any party with standing that is adversely affected. No statutory comment requirement outside FAST-41.
- epra: No change.
- speed: Only a party that filed a substantive and unique comment and suffers direct harm. No challenges to the creation of a categorical exclusion.
  Source: [Sec. 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%203.%20JUDICIAL%20REVIEW)
- senate: Only a party alleging an actual or imminent injury amounting to direct harm. Where a comment period was offered, it must also have filed a detailed substantive comment.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Which court

- current: District court, unless another statute sends the case to a court of appeals.
- epra: No change.
- speed: No change.
- senate: The court of appeals for the circuit where the project sits, with randomly assigned judges.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Remedy for a flawed review

- current: Courts may vacate the approval or enjoin the project.
- epra: Ordinary remedies. An agency gets no more than 180 days on remand.
  Source: [Sec. 101](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20101.%20ACCELERATING%20CLAIMS)
- speed: Remand only, without vacatur or injunction, with a fix due in 180 days. Applies to earlier court orders too.
  Source: [Sec. 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%203.%20JUDICIAL%20REVIEW)
- senate: Remand only, without vacatur or injunction, with a fix due in 180 days. Work may continue during the remand. A preliminary injunction is possible when a different federal law is likely violated.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Court timetable

- current: None.
- epra: Expedited consideration.
  Source: [Sec. 101](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20101.%20ACCELERATING%20CLAIMS)
- speed: Judgment within 180 days of the agency record. Appeals decided in 180 days.
  Source: [Sec. 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%203.%20JUDICIAL%20REVIEW)
- senate: Final judgment 'as expeditiously as possible'. No fixed deadline.
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
### Suits over energy and mineral permits under any law

- current: 6 years by default.
- epra: 150 days. Remand capped at 180 days.
  Source: [Sec. 101](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20101.%20ACCELERATING%20CLAIMS)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: 150 days. Remand capped at 180 days.
  Bill: [2201](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2201.md)
### Suits under water, wildlife and historic preservation laws

- current: 6 years, in district court, with ordinary remedies.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: 150 days for section 404 permits, biological opinions and section 106 decisions. Biological opinions go to the D.C. Circuit. Remand without vacatur for section 404 and section 106.
  Bill: [1205](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1205.md)
  Bill: [1305](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1305.md)
  Bill: [2301](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2301.md)
### Revoking an issued permit

- current: Allowed under each statute and permit, subject to ordinary court review.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Barred except for a court order, breach, fraud, a specific and immediate harm, or the holder's request. Review in the court of appeals. The bill sets out no money damages.
  Source: [Sec. 2(b)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Barred, with the same five exceptions, for permits in effect on or after September 16, 2026. The agency carries the burden by clear and convincing evidence. A winning sponsor recovers fees, delay costs and 25 to 50 percent of project costs.
  Bill: [1401](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1401.md)
### Approvals reopened since January 2025

- current: Agencies may ask a court to send their own approvals back.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Exempt. The bill does not apply to any action an agency moved to reconsider after January 20, 2025.
  Source: [Sec. 4](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%204.%20PRESERVATION%20OF%20ONGOING%20ADMINISTRATIVE%20CORRECTIONS)
- senate: No exemption. Where a stop-work order from the year before enactment was enjoined, the same judge hears any new attempt.
  Bill: [1401](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1401.md)
### Unequal treatment of energy types

- current: No cause of action.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Applicants in 46 named project types, plus any similar type a court certifies, can sue over an intentional pattern of delays or denials aimed at their project type. Damages run from 50 to 100 percent of expected construction cost.
  Bill: [1402](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1402.md)
### Permits that need no environmental document

- current: No general deadline.
- epra: No general deadline. Clocks for particular permits only, such as wind, solar and geothermal applications.
  Source: [Secs. 206, 208](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20206.%20ACCELERATING%20RENEWABLE%20ENERGY%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Decision within 1 year of a complete application for the listed project types, enforceable in court.
  Bill: [1402](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1402.md)
  Bill: [1403](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1403.md)
### State water quality certification

- current: States certify compliance with water quality standards and other appropriate state law within a reasonable period of up to 1 year.
  Source: [33 U.S.C. 1341](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/33/1341)
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Scope limited to water quality requirements. Denials and conditions need clear and convincing evidence. One-year cap, extendable only if the applicant and the state both agree in writing. Interstate pipelines and transmission lines get 9 months and are reviewed only for direct point-source discharges.
  Bill: [1202](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1202.md)
### Clean Water Act permits

- current: EPA may veto a fill site at any time. Nationwide permits and state discharge permits last 5 years. A 2020 court ruling required wildlife consultation to reissue a nationwide permit.
  Source: [33 U.S.C. 1342, 1344](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/33/1342)
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: EPA veto limited to the period between a complete application and the permit. Nationwide and discharge permits last 10 years. Nationwide permits that keep their preconstruction requirements are reissued without consultation, and fills under 2 acres count as minimal.
  Bill: [1203](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1203.md)
  Bill: [1204](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1204.md)
### Endangered species consultation

- current: Formal consultation in 90 days, extendable. Only the federal wildlife agencies issue biological opinions.
  Source: [16 U.S.C. 1536](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/16/1536)
- epra: No change to consultation. Interior's approval of tribal right-of-way rules is exempt from the Act.
  Source: [Sec. 205](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20205.%20RIGHTS-OF-WAY%20ACROSS%20INDIAN%20LAND)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: 60 days, and no later than the NEPA deadline absent extraordinary circumstances. States may take over consultation under an agreement with Interior. $150 million a year authorized.
  Bill: [1302](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1302.md)
  Bill: [1304](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1304.md)
  Bill: [1307](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1307.md)
### Historic preservation review

- current: Agencies 'take into account' effects on historic properties under Advisory Council rules. No statutory deadlines. Visual and audible effects count.
  Source: [54 U.S.C. 306108; 36 CFR part 800](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/54/306108)
- epra: No change to the review. Interior's approval of tribal right-of-way rules is exempt from it.
  Source: [Sec. 205](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20205.%20RIGHTS-OF-WAY%20ACROSS%20INDIAN%20LAND)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Statutory deadlines from start to finish. Adverse effects limited to direct alteration. Loans and grants alone do not trigger review. An agency may proceed when a preservation officer is silent for 30 days.
  Bill: [2301](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2301.md)
### Federal siting of interstate lines

- current: FERC can site a line only inside a corridor the Energy Department has designated, and only where a state lacks authority, has held an application for more than 1 year, or has set uneconomic conditions.
  Source: [16 U.S.C. 824p](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/16/824p)
- epra: FERC may permit lines of 100 kilovolts and up without a corridor.
  Source: [Sec. 401](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20401.%20TRANSMISSION%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: FERC shall permit lines of 230 kilovolts and up without a corridor. The state's clock starts on the day the application is filed with the state. Developers of lines of 345 kilovolts and up may file at FERC and the state together.
  Bill: [2101](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2101.md)
### Regional and interregional planning

- current: Regional planning required by FERC Orders 1000 and 1920. Interregional work is coordination only.
- epra: Joint interregional plans required within 2 years. FERC resolves disputes and can impose a plan.
  Source: [Sec. 402](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20402.%20TRANSMISSION%20PLANNING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Regional and interregional planning processes required within 2 years. Order No. 1920 compliance counts for the regional part. FERC can extend a late filing by 6 months.
  Bill: [2103](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2103.md)
### Who pays for new lines

- current: Beneficiaries pay, roughly in proportion to benefits, under FERC and court precedent.
- epra: Beneficiaries pay under the cost-causation principle. No involuntary charges for trivial benefits.
  Source: [Secs. 401, 402](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20401.%20TRANSMISSION%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Same rule, with costs 'at least roughly commensurate' with six listed benefits.
  Bill: [2101](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2101.md)
  Bill: [2103](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2103.md)
### Upgrades in existing corridors

- current: Covered by agency categorical exclusions in some cases.
- epra: Interior and Agriculture adopt categorical exclusions within 180 days.
  Source: [Sec. 209](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20209.%20ELECTRIC%20GRID%20PROJECTS)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Reconductoring, voltage increases and added circuits in existing rights-of-way are outside NEPA and section 106 by statute. So are gas pipeline looping and compression in existing corridors.
  Bill: [2102](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2102.md)
  Bill: [2214](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2214.md)
### Data centers and other large loads

- current: No federal floor. Retail costs are set in state rate cases and utility tariffs. FERC's 1994 transmission pricing policy lets a utility charge a new transmission customer the higher of embedded cost or incremental expansion cost, not the sum of the two. It may price separate lines on different bases.
  Source: [FERC pricing policy statement, 59 FR 55031 (1994)](https://archives.federalregister.gov/issue_slice/1994/11/3/55026-55045.pdf)
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: New Federal Power Act section 228 covers data center and high-density computing loads of 20 megawatts or more, counting phased buildouts and commonly controlled sites. Those that connect after enactment pay the full incremental cost of serving them, even after they leave; arrangements approved earlier stay in effect. States may auction access, require new generation, and require curtailable service. Separately, and with no size threshold, FERC must charge computing loads both the embedded and the incremental cost of transmission service. The Energy Information Administration must collect data center load.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
  Bill: [2114](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2114.md)
- note: The Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) would ask state regulators to consider making data centers of 100 megawatts or more pay the full incremental cost of upgrades, including after they leave, with financial assurance before construction. States would not have to adopt it. It passed the House 417-3 on September 16, 2026, and the Senate rejected cloture 57-43 on September 30. BAAJA section 228 uses similar terms but makes them binding at 20 megawatts, and section 2107(a) adds an embedded-cost charge for transmission. Harvard's Ari Peskoe called the House bill's consider standard 'largely symbolic', since Congress cannot force state regulators to act, and called BAAJA's data center rules 'an improvement on the status quo'.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, as passed by the House](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Source: [CBS News on the 417-3 House vote](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/house-bill-data-center-energy-costs/)
  Source: [Senate roll call vote 254](https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1192/vote_119_2_00254.htm)
  Source: [Heatmap on the Ratepayer Protection Act](https://heatmap.news/politics/ratepayer-protection-act-explained)
  Source: [Heatmap on the Senate bill's data center rules](https://heatmap.news/daily/data-center-permitting-deal)
### Interconnection queues

- current: Cluster studies under FERC Order No. 2023.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Interconnection planned with transmission over 20 years, with published per-megawatt prices and nonrefundable deposits. Automation required in queue studies. Grid data due in 15 days.
  Bill: [2106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2106.md)
  Bill: [2110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2110.md)
  Bill: [2111](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2111.md)
### Advanced transmission technologies

- current: Planners must consider them under Order No. 1920.
- epra: Advanced conductors eligible for backstop permits.
  Source: [Sec. 401](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20401.%20TRANSMISSION%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Utilities must deploy them when benefits exceed costs, or face a lower return on equity.
  Bill: [2109](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2109.md)
### Right of first refusal

- current: FERC removed the federal right in 2011 and allowed it again for some replacement lines in Order No. 1920.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Banned for regionally or interregionally planned lines.
  Bill: [2105](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2105.md)
### Local transmission spending

- current: Little federal review of projects a utility plans for itself.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: States can refer a utility to FERC. Remedies include a lower return and fines up to $5 million per facility.
  Bill: [2104](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2104.md)
### Customer-sited batteries and generators

- current: Wholesale market access by rule under FERC Order No. 2222.
- epra: Not addressed.
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Statutory wholesale market access for aggregations of 100 kilowatts and up, with a ban on double payment.
  Bill: [2108](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2108.md)
### Oil and gas

- current: A federal drilling permit is required whenever a well taps federal minerals. Five routine activities get a rebuttable categorical exclusion.
  Source: [30 U.S.C. 226; 42 U.S.C. 15942](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/30/226)
- epra: No federal permit where the federal mineral share is under 50 percent on non-federal land. Lease nominations offered as submitted. Drilling permits last 4 years.
  Source: [Secs. 201 to 203](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20201.%20ONSHORE%20OIL%20AND%20GAS%20LEASING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: No federal permit where the federal mineral share is under 50 percent on non-federal land. The five routine activities are outside NEPA entirely.
  Bill: [2211](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2211.md)
  Bill: [2229](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2229.md)
### Coal

- current: Leasing at Interior's discretion, with no decision deadlines.
- epra: Deadlines for coal lease reviews and decisions.
  Source: [Sec. 204](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20204.%20COAL%20LEASES%20ON%20FEDERAL%20LAND)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: No leasing provisions. Coal appears only in the list of project types protected from unequal treatment.
  Bill: [1402](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1402.md)
### Wind, solar and storage on public land

- current: No application deadlines. A 2020 goal of 25 gigawatts by 2025.
  Source: [43 U.S.C. 3004](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/43/3004)
- epra: 30-day clocks, small-project exclusions, and a goal of 50 gigawatts by 2030.
  Source: [Secs. 206, 207](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20206.%20ACCELERATING%20RENEWABLE%20ENERGY%20PERMITTING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: The same 30-day clocks and small-project exclusions. No gigawatt goal.
  Bill: [2213](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2213.md)
### Offshore leasing

- current: Offshore wind leasing is tied to oil and gas lease sales by the Inflation Reduction Act.
  Source: [43 U.S.C. 3006(b)(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/43/3006)
- epra: One oil and gas sale and one wind sale every year through 2029, 400,000 acres of wind a year, and a 30-gigawatt wind goal.
  Source: [Secs. 301, 302](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20301.%20OFFSHORE%20OIL%20AND%20GAS%20LEASING)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: No lease sale mandates. Changes Interior's offshore wind test to 'unreasonable interference' with other uses and orders planned offshore transmission routes.
  Bill: [2251](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2251.md)
  Bill: [2252](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2252.md)
### LNG exports

- current: Energy Department public-interest review with no deadline.
  Source: [15 U.S.C. 717b](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/717b)
- epra: Decision within 90 days of the environmental review, or the application is deemed granted.
  Source: [Secs. 601, 602](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20601.%20ACTION%20ON%20APPLICATIONS)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: No export provisions. LNG projects appear in the list of project types protected from unequal treatment.
  Bill: [1402](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1402.md)
### Geothermal

- current: Lease sales at least every 2 years.
  Source: [30 U.S.C. 1003](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/30/1003)
- epra: Annual lease sales, 30-day permit decisions, an ombudsman, and exclusions for test wells.
  Source: [Sec. 208](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20208.%20GEOTHERMAL%20LEASING%20AND%20PERMITTING%20IMPROVEMENTS)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: All of that, plus a per-plant royalty clock, no federal permit on minority-interest land, processing during lawsuits, and a NEPA exemption for routine drilling.
  Bill: [2221](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2221.md)
  Bill: [2222](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2222.md)
  Bill: [2223](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2223.md)
  Bill: [2224](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2224.md)
  Bill: [2225](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2225.md)
  Bill: [2226](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2226.md)
  Bill: [2229](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2229.md)
### Hydropower

- current: Federal land agencies set mandatory license conditions.
  Source: [16 U.S.C. 797(e)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/16/797)
- epra: License extensions, a market barriers report, and aligned timetables.
  Source: [Secs. 701 to 703](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20701.%20HYDROPOWER%20LICENSE%20EXTENSIONS)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: The market barriers report, a limit on mandatory conditions, no approval for routine maintenance, and a 1-year deadline for FERC to decide small hydrokinetic licenses.
  Bill: [2231](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2231.md)
  Bill: [2232](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2232.md)
  Bill: [2233](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2233.md)
  Bill: [2234](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2234.md)
### Hardrock mining

- current: Mill sites are capped at 5 acres each. A 2022 appeals court ruling barred waste storage on claims without valuable minerals.
  Source: [30 U.S.C. 42](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/30/42)
- epra: As many mill sites as reasonably necessary, with fees paid into a cleanup fund.
  Source: [Sec. 210](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20210.%20HARDROCK%20MINING%20MILL%20SITES)
- speed: Not addressed.
- senate: Same as EPRA 2024.
  Bill: [2215](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2215.md)
### Tribal lands

- current: Interior must approve rights-of-way across tribal land.
  Source: [25 U.S.C. 323 to 328](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/25/323)
- epra: Tribes may grant their own rights-of-way under approved tribal rules.
  Source: [Sec. 205](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-118s4753rs/html/BILLS-118s4753rs.htm#:~:text=SEC.%20205.%20RIGHTS-OF-WAY%20ACROSS%20INDIAN%20LAND)
- speed: No NEPA suits over tribal trust resource projects except by the tribe. The no-action alternative is presumed harmful for tribe-initiated projects.
  Source: [Secs. 2(b), 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr4776eh/html/BILLS-119hr4776eh.htm#:~:text=SEC.%202.%20NEPA%20REFORM)
- senate: Both: tribal rights-of-way, the limit on NEPA suits, and the no-action presumption.
  Bill: [2212](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2212.md)
  Bill: [1110](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1110.md)
  Bill: [1106](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/1106.md)

## Data center bills

BAAJA's data center rules beside the federal bills that would make large computing loads pay for the grid they use. Each cell links to the text it summarizes.

- Current policy: The White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge (March 2026) and FERC's June 18, 2026 show cause orders. FERC set no large-load rule. [Current policy](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
- BAAJA: Released September 30, 2026. Sections 2107 and 2114. [BAAJA](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2026/9/capito-lee-whitehouse-and-heinrich-introduce-bipartisan-american-affordability-and-jobs-act-of-2026)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Evans (R-Colo.) and Castor (D-Fla.). House-passed text, September 16, 2026. Senate cloture failed September 30; vote sources are in the large-load comparison note. [Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Heinrich (D-N.M.), August 2026. In committee; a unanimous-consent request failed September 17. [GRID Savings Act (S. 5199)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Van Hollen (D-Md.), January 2026; House companion H.R. 8241 (Tonko). In committee. [Power for the People Act (S. 3682)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Hawley (R-Mo.) and Blumenthal (D-Conn.), February 11, 2026. In committee. [GRID Act (S. 3852)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)

### Who is covered

- Current policy: The Pledge: seven hyperscalers and AI companies, later joined by governors, developers and power providers. FERC's June 2026 orders: the six regional grid operators.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "President Trump is calling on the leading United States hyperscalers and AI companies to build, bring, or buy all of the energy needed for building and operating data centers"
- BAAJA: Section 228: data centers and high-density computing, including crypto mining, of 20 MW or more at one site or at commonly controlled sites, counting phased buildouts. Section 2107(a) pricing: any computational load on the bulk-power system, no size threshold. Ancillary computing at other commercial or industrial facilities is excluded from section 228.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Data centers with 100 MW or more of peak demand at one site or campus, contracting after enactment. The introduced bill covered any 100 MW load; committee narrowed it.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "require electric energy primarily to operate information technology infrastructure and related systems pertaining to data storage and computational applications and services"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Any new or expanded non-residential load of 150 MW or more at one interconnection, counting affiliated sites and phases. Not limited to data centers.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "has an aggregate requested or projected peak electric demand of not less than 150 megawatts behind a single point of interconnection"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Data centers drawing more than 50 MW, counting same-owner facilities in one utility area. Crypto mines are defined separately.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "has an energy demand greater than 50 megawatts"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Private data centers of 20 MW or more, existing or planned within 5 years. Federal data centers excluded.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "with a power demand of 20 megawatts or more that is not owned, operated, or maintained"

### Binding or optional

- Current policy: Mostly voluntary. The Pledge creates no legal duty. FERC's June 18 orders find grid operators' tariffs may be unjust and make them justify or rewrite them. No final FERC rule.
  Source: [Proclamation, 91 FR 11439](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge-proclamation)
  Quote: "The Ratepayer Protection Pledge and the commitments embodied therein effectuate the national policy of the United States."
- BAAJA: Binding. Section 228 is a federal floor in the Federal Power Act. Section 2107(a) orders FERC to revise its 1994 pricing policy in 270 days, propose a rule 270 days later and finish within a year.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Optional. A PURPA standard each state must consider within 1 year and decide within 2. States need not adopt it.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "shall commence consideration under section 111, or set a hearing date for consideration"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Binding. New Federal Power Act section 224 gives FERC jurisdiction over large-load interconnection; final rule within 1 year.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "the Commission shall issue a final rule, applicable to each transmitting utility, establishing standards and procedures for the interconnection of covered large loads"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Mixed. FERC must order transmission cost tariffs (120 days) and a data center queue rule (180 days). The rate class is a PURPA standard states must consider.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "the Commission shall issue a rule requiring all covered interconnection entities to create, for the purpose of addressing reliability and affordability concerns from new data center loads"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Binding prohibition enforced by DOE, with penalties of at least $1 million a day.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "a covered entity may not build, own, operate, or maintain a data center unless the data center derives all of its energy"

### Cost of serving the load

- Current policy: Pledge signers say they will pay for the new generation and grid upgrades their data centers need. Retail costs otherwise follow state rate cases.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "Companies will pay for all new power delivery infrastructure upgrades required to service their data centers"
- BAAJA: No incremental cost of serving a covered load (generation, storage, transmission, distribution) may be recovered from other customers.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Rates recover from the data center the full incremental cost of generation, transmission or distribution upgrades needed to serve it.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "shall be designed to recover from the large-load customer the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve the load of such large-load customer"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): The load pays all interconnection and direct-assignment costs. Network upgrades are charged to it and credited back against its transmission bills, as for generators. Generation and distribution are not covered.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "directly assigned to, and fully borne by, the applicable covered large-load customer"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Data centers pay local transmission upgrades that exist only because of them. States must consider a rate class that recovers the full cost of upgrades.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "allocate to each interconnecting data center local transmission upgrade costs that, but for the existence of the data center, would not be needed"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): No cost allocation rule. New data centers must be off the grid; existing ones must show they do not raise rates or pay credits.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "will not increase the electrical rates paid by ratepayers"

### Transmission pricing

- Current policy: FERC's 1994 transmission pricing policy allows the higher of embedded cost or incremental expansion cost for a service, rather than their sum. Separate lines may be priced on different bases.
  Source: [FERC pricing policy statement, 59 FR 55031 (1994)](https://archives.federalregister.gov/issue_slice/1994/11/3/55026-55045.pdf)
- BAAJA: Computational loads pay both the embedded and the incremental cost of transmission. Incremental payments are credited to the utility's revenue requirement so other customers are not charged twice.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Transmission upgrades fall under the state standard. No FERC role and no embedded-cost charge.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve the load of such large-load customer"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): FERC classifies and allocates facilities under interconnection rules adapted for loads. A load may fund regional lines in exchange for transmission rights.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "to voluntarily fund all or a portion of a transmission facility selected in a regional or interregional transmission plan"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Two parts: direct assignment of local upgrades, plus rates reflecting the embedded cost of the grid.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "require data centers to pay transmission rates applicable to their rate class that reflect the embedded cost of the integrated grid"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): No transmission pricing rule and no FERC role.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "how interconnection costs and other infrastructure costs needed to supply the data center with power from the electric grid are allocated"

### If the data center leaves

- Current policy: Pledge signers say they will pay negotiated rates whether or not they use the power.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "Importantly, they will pay these rates for the power and related infrastructure that are brought online to service their data centers, whether they use the electricity or not"
- BAAJA: Recovery continues if the data center ends its contract or stops buying power before the incremental cost is paid off.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Recovery continues if the customer ends its contract or stops buying power.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "including in the event of such large-load customer terminating a contract or other agreement with the electric utility"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Financial security must protect other customers if the load fails to proceed or perform.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "financial security designed to protect any customer from unrecovered costs if a covered large load fails to proceed or perform"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): States must consider longer minimum contracts and minimum demand charges.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "an extension of minimum utility contract lengths for data center customers to ensure that data center load does not leave utilities and ratepayers with stranded costs"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Not addressed.

### Up-front collateral

- Current policy: FERC's June orders call for rising readiness requirements to deter speculative requests.
  Source: [Utility Dive on FERC's June 2026 orders](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/)
  Quote: "We target speculative projects by establishing escalating readiness requirements for distinct phases of the study process to deter duplicative or speculative requests for transmission service,"
- BAAJA: Before building or upgrading generation, transmission or distribution for the load, the utility must collect assurances or contributions covering the cost.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): The utility must require assurances or contributions before building an upgrade.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "an electric utility shall require the large-load customer provide to the electric utility financial assurances or contributions to cover the cost of such upgrade"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): FERC's rule sets payment and security requirements.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "financial security designed to protect any customer from unrecovered costs if a covered large load fails to proceed or perform"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): States must consider higher study fees, deposits or collateral, and up-front construction contributions.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "an increase in up-front interconnection study costs, deposit amounts, or collateral requirements for data center projects"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Not addressed.

### Separate rate class

- Current policy: Pledge signers say they will negotiate separate rate structures with utilities and states.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "Companies will voluntarily negotiate new, separate rate structures with their utilities and relevant State governments wherever they build data centers."
- BAAJA: States may make data centers a separate class with rates, terms and interconnection priorities less favorable than other large industrial loads.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Not addressed.
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): States must consider a data center rate class. DOE grants help them.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "establishing a rate class specific to data centers to ensure that data center owners and operators are covering the full cost of the generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades necessary to serve data centers"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): DOE must put residential customers' rates ahead of every other class.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "the Secretary shall prioritize the electrical rates paid by residential ratepayers over all other ratepayer classes"

### Who connects first

- Current policy: FERC wants standard large-load applications and studies in each region.
  Source: [RMI on FERC's June 2026 orders](https://rmi.org/resources/understanding-fercs-large-load-orders/)
  Quote: "Develop standardized transmission service applications and study processes for large loads"
- BAAJA: States may run open seasons that award service by greatest benefit to other ratepayers, whatever the order of requests.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Study timelines and readiness requirements against speculative requests. No open seasons.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "protect other customers from the costs of speculative or duplicative requests"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Grid operators run a data center queue that favors those offsetting their demand, and may delay or deny connections that hurt reliability or affordability.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "a data center that is not already interconnected with the electric grid may not interconnect with the electric grid unless the data center has fully advanced through the applicable data center load queue system"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Not addressed.

### Bring your own power

- Current policy: Pledge signers say they will build, bring or buy new generation. FERC told grid operators to address co-location.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "Companies will build, bring, or buy the new generation resources and electricity needed to satisfy their new energy demands"
- BAAJA: States may require the data center to procure, build or contract for new generation sufficient to serve it.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Optional. A load may be studied with its own generation, storage or flexibility.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "the study and interconnection, separately or together, of a covered large load and any associated generation, energy storage, or verifiable load flexibility"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Queue priority for data centers that bring new low- or no-carbon supply they pay for. Not required.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "are designated for the service of, and paid for by, the data center owner or operator, including through a power purchase agreement or another bilateral contract"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Starting 180 days after enactment, new data centers must take all power, including backup, from sources separate from the grid. Existing grid-connected centers have a 10-year transition under DOE certificates.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "derives all of its energy, including back-up energy, from a captive power plant, on-site power generation, or some other source or combination of sources separate from, and not deriving power from, the electric grid"

### Curtailable service

- Current policy: FERC asked grid operators for new transmission services for flexible large loads.
  Source: [Utility Dive on FERC's June 2026 orders](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/)
  Quote: "new transmission services for flexible large loads"
- BAAJA: States may require service that limits how much or when the load draws power. FERC must price non-firm transmission service lower.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Flexible and phased interconnection service at the customer's election.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "flexible interconnection service, subject to enforceable operating limits"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Flexibility agreements let the operator curtail data centers before other users and can count toward the supply they must bring.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "data centers may be interrupted by the covered interconnection entity"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Not addressed.

### Surplus returned to other customers

- Current policy: Not addressed.
- BAAJA: States may charge more than cost and credit the surplus to other customers.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Upgrade payments are credited back to the paying load, not to other customers.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "those costs shall be credited back against transmission service charges"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): Not addressed.
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Grid-connected data centers can pay Rate Effect Credits to offset their effect on rates.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "a credit paid by a covered entity to an appropriate party, as determined by the Secretary, that offsets the effect that a data center would otherwise have on the electrical rates paid by ratepayers"

### Existing data centers

- Current policy: The Pledge covers new demand only.
  Source: [White House, Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/03/ratepayer-protection-pledge/)
  Quote: "satisfy their new energy demands"
- BAAJA: Section 228(b) cost protection and (c) state open-season authority apply to covered loads interconnecting on or after enactment. Previously approved service arrangements remain in effect. Section 2107(a) transmission pricing has no express existing-load exemption; its scope is separate.
  Bill: [2107](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2107.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Applies to customers that request service or contract after enactment. States that already acted on a comparable standard are exempt.
  Source: [H.R. 9340, House-passed text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9340eh/html/BILLS-119hr9340eh.htm)
  Quote: "on or after the date of the enactment of this paragraph, requests to enter into, or enters into, a contract or other agreement"
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): New or expanded loads only.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "a new or expanded nonresidential electric load"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): The queue covers data centers not yet connected. The text does not say how the tariff or rate class treats existing sites.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "a data center that is not already interconnected with the electric grid may not interconnect"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): Existing data centers get 10 years to leave the grid, operating meanwhile under one-year DOE certificates.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "Until the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment of this Act, a covered entity that owns, operates, or maintains an existing data center that derives any of its energy from the electric grid"

### Reporting

- Current policy: FERC found grid operators' upgrade costs are not transparent. No EIA change.
  Source: [Utility Dive on FERC's June 2026 orders](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/)
  Quote: "lack of transparency in how RTOs and ISOs determine how network upgrades are assigned and paid for"
- BAAJA: EIA must add data center load to Form 861, with no 20 MW threshold in section 2114. Revision is due at least 90 days before the first April 1 after enactment.
  Bill: [2114](https://pranava0x0.github.io/permittingreform/sections/2114.md)
- Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340): Not addressed.
- GRID Savings Act (S. 5199): Each load, state commission and FERC get the classification, costs and alternatives studied.
  Source: [S. 5199 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5199is/html/BILLS-119s5199is.htm)
  Quote: "Disclosure to the applicable covered large-load customer, each applicable State commission, and the Commission of"
- Power for the People Act (S. 3682): FERC sets disclosure rules for interconnection requests. DOE helps with load forecasts.
  Source: [S. 3682 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3682is/html/BILLS-119s3682is.htm)
  Quote: "the Commission shall establish transparency and disclosure requirements for data center load interconnection requests"
- GRID Act (S. 3852): DOE sets public disclosure of usage, property deals and utility agreements.
  Source: [S. 3852 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3852is/html/BILLS-119s3852is.htm)
  Quote: "the Secretary shall establish a national requirement for covered entities to provide to the public"
